origins.section: The Month Model Promises Work One Crew Cannot Do, and Refuses Work One Crew Can
A Trim Is an Optional Interval on Each Crew, and a Crew's Intervals Never Overlap
Five New Tests, and Two Old Ones Retire

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-six-weeks: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-six-weeks: month model     a 6-week trim, 1 crew, 2 months: not trimmed -- 'it refuses the trim, because no single month holds 6 crew-weeks'
recorded.prompt:q-absent: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-absent: when the literal is false the interval is "simply ignored by all constraints", in the words of the new_optional_fixed_size_interval_var docstring
recorded.prompt:q-retire: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-retire: Two of the month tests retire, because they test months, which no longer exist; their rule survives in new tests.
